title: Fork pull request's remote-execution build was rejected: BuildBuddy API key secret was empty
summary: The windows-remote-exec job, from a workflow added by fork pull request #30121, ran 'bazelisk build --config=remote' with --remote_header=x-buildbuddy-api-key=$env:BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY. The job had no secrets ('Secret source: None', BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY empty), so BuildBuddy rejected the remote download of rules_python with PERMISSION_DENIED: Missing API key. Every run of this workflow on the pull request, June to October 2026, failed.
recommendation: Do not run credentialed remote builds on pull_request events from forks: skip the job (or fall back to a local build) when the API key is empty, and run the remote build only where secrets are available, such as after merge or on a maintainer-approved trigger. Never expose the key to untrusted fork code.
evidence: Error in download_and_extract: java.io.IOException: io.grpc.StatusRuntimeException: PERMISSION_DENIED: Missing API key
root_cause: The workflow passes BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY from repository secrets to Bazel as an x-buildbuddy-api-key header, but GitHub does not give secrets to pull_request workflows from forks. The job ran with no secrets ('Secret source: None') and an empty BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY, so BuildBuddy refused the remote download with PERMISSION_DENIED: Missing API key.

fix.description: No fix yet: the pull request is open and every run of the workflow has failed. Proposed: skip or fall back to a local build when the key is empty, and run the remote build only where secrets are available.
